key_insight: Chemical disorder in Nb₀.₄₅Ta₀.₂₅Ti₀.₁₅Hf₀.₁₅ supports robust superconductivity, strong vortex pinning, and signatures of enhanced electronic correlations.
engineering_relevance: This mechanically robust medium-entropy alloy offers a promising route toward superconductors that combine current-carrying capability with structural durability.
method: Specific-heat analysis of pairing and electron–phonon coupling.
Disorder-explicit density functional theory of phase stability, electronic states, and local distortion.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a superconducting onset near 7.8 K, Jc = 0.48 × 10⁶ A/cm², electron–phonon coupling λ = 1.07, and calculated local lattice distortion Δd = 0.086 Å.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify the temperature and magnetic field for the reported critical current density, limiting application-level comparisons.
paper_title: Interplay of Chemical Disorder, Vortex Pinning, and Electron Correlations in the Mechanically Robust Medium-Entropy Alloy Superconductor $\text{Nb}_{0.45}\text{Ta}_{0.25}\text{Ti}_{0.15}\text{Hf}_{0.15}$
